questions.q: A user orders 2 units of the same "New Software License" catalog item in one checkout. What records does that create?
options: Two separate sc_req_item records, one per license
Two sc_request records, each with one sc_req_item
One sc_request and one sc_req_item record, with the sc_req_item's quantity field set to 2
One sc_req_item record with no sc_request at all
questions.explain: Ordering 2 units of the same item in one cart is one line item with quantity 2, not two separate Requested Item records.

questions.q: In the lab's design, why is the Open to Work in Progress transition a human-fulfilled step rather than automatic?
options: Because IT licensing must acknowledge budget and seat availability before any provisioning starts
Because Flow Designer cannot automate any part of this process
Because Open and Work in Progress mean the same thing
Because the requester must manually set the state themselves
questions.explain: A real business reason — confirming budget/seats — justifies gating the transition behind a human acknowledgment.

questions.q: What must the fulfillment flow confirm before setting the Requested Item to Closed Complete?
options: That the requester has replied to a satisfaction survey
Nothing beyond successfully sending the REST request
That the REST response actually confirms success, such as a returned license_ids array matching the requested quantity
That 24 hours have passed since the request was submitted
questions.explain: Closing on a sent request rather than a confirmed, matching response risks marking unprovisioned licenses as done.

questions.q: What should the flow do if the external licensing system returns fewer seats than were requested?
options: Close the item as Closed Complete anyway, since some seats were provisioned
Delete the Requested Item and have the user re-submit
Ignore the discrepancy since quantity doesn't affect fulfillment
Route the item back to Work in Progress with a note describing what the API actually returned, instead of closing it
questions.explain: A partial or mismatched result is not full success — the item needs human attention, not a silent close.

questions.q: What design mistake does this lab's flow specifically avoid?
options: Using Flow Designer instead of legacy Workflow
Assigning the request to the IT Licensing group
Closing the Requested Item as soon as the REST call is sent, instead of waiting for and checking the actual response
Letting the Request roll up its state from its Requested Items
questions.explain: Closing on a sent call rather than a confirmed response is exactly the shortcut that would let a failed provisioning silently read as done.
